### required packages

```{r packages, warning = FALSE, error = FALSE}
### handling missing data

### visualizing regression

```

## Read data from other sources
```{r read data from other sources}
data_spss <- read_sav("data_spss.sav")
data_sas <- read_xpt("data_sas.xpt")

data_excel <- read_excel("data_all.xlsx", sheet = "data_all")
```

## Missing data
```{r exploring missing data 1}
# NaN (Not a Number): NA means the value is missing. NaN means a calculation did not produce a defined numerical value
x <- log(c(1, -1, NA))
x
is.nan(x)

# Inf (infinite numbers)
y <- c(-Inf, 0, Inf)
is.infinite(y)
```

```{r exploring missing data 2}
data_missing <- read_csv("data_missing.csv")
missing_table <- miss_var_summary(data_missing)
missing_table

#visualize entire dataframe
vis_dat(data_missing)
```

## Data Wrangling
```{r data wrangling}
data1 <- read_csv("dataset1.csv")
data2 <- read_csv("dataset2.csv")
data3 <- read_csv("dataset3.csv")
data4 <- read_csv("dataset4.csv")

# merge dataset
data_all <- bind_rows(data1, data2, data3, data4)
```

```{r advanced}
# find csv files whose names match the pattern
paths <- list.files(pattern = "dataset.*\\.csv", full.names = TRUE)
paths

# read each file and store the resulting dataset in a list
files <- map(paths, read_csv)
length(files) # check how many files were read and stored

# stack the datasets by rows (rbind)
data_test <- list_rbind(files) # when we use join, it matches with a key such as ID. Here, it's more like appending the dataset in rows from multiple files
summary(data_test)
```

```{r join by ID}
names_data <- read_csv("names.csv")
glimpse(names_data) # we inspect the dataset: dimensions, column names, types, and values

# left_join keeps all rows in the first dataset, and add columns from names_data, and they match rows using 'id' field
# left_join(): keeps all rows from the left dataset
# full_join(): keeps all rows from both datasets
data_all <- left_join(data_all, names_data, by = join_by(id))
table(data_all$parent)
```

## Data Visualization

```{r data viz 1 bar graph}
data_all <- data_all %>%
  mutate(stroke_recode = case_when(
    stroke == "1" ~ "Yes",
    stroke == "0" ~ "No"
  ))

data_all$stroke_recode <- as_factor(data_all$stroke_recode)
table(data_all$stroke, data_all$stroke_recode)

bar_stroke <- ggplot(data_all, aes(stroke_recode)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Has had a stroke") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0)) 
# you can change font, background, legend, grid, etc with theme
plot(bar_stroke)
```

```{r ggplot theme}
bar_stroke <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = stroke_recode)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Stroke History",
    x = "Has had a stroke",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
plot(bar_stroke)

bar_stroke + theme_minimal()
bar_stroke + theme_classic()
bar_stroke + theme_bw()
```

```{r data viz 2 box plot}
# single var box plot
boxplot <- ggplot(data_all, aes(stroke_recode)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  coord_flip()

plot(boxplot)

# box plot is most effective in showing the distribution of one 'continuous' variable
boxplot <- ggplot(data_all, aes(age)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Age") +
  theme_classic()

plot(boxplot)

# two vars box plot
boxplot_stroke <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = stroke_recode, colour = stroke_recode)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  coord_flip() +
  theme_classic()

plot(boxplot_stroke)
```

```{r data viz 3 scatter plot}
scatter_plot <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1)) +
  geom_point()
plot(scatter_plot)

scatter_plot <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1)) +
  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.2, # alpha controls transparency 
    position = position_jitter()) # jitter reveals overlapping obs by slightly shifting their plotted position
plot(scatter_plot)

scatter_plot <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1)) +
  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.2, # alpha controls transparency 
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.3, height = 0, seed =123)) # here, we only shift point horizontally, keeping LDL value (y) unchanged
plot(scatter_plot)

# regression line
scatter_plot_line <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter()) +
  geom_smooth(color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#088da5")
plot(scatter_plot_line)

scatter_plot_line2 <- scatter_plot +
  geom_smooth(color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#088da5")
plot(scatter_plot_line2)

scatter_plot_line3 <- scatter_plot +
  geom_smooth(color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#088da5", se = FALSE)
plot(scatter_plot_line3)
```

```{r changing the axis labels}
scatter_plot_variables <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter()) +
  geom_smooth(color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#088da5") +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL Cholesterol")
plot(scatter_plot_variables)

scatter_plot_variables2 <- scatter_plot_line +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL Cholesterol")
plot(scatter_plot_variables2)
```

```{r changing the shading of the points}
scatter_plot_alpha <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, position = position_jitter()) +
  geom_smooth(color = "red") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#088da5") + 
  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL cholesterol")
plot(scatter_plot_alpha)
```

```{r grouping with ggplot2}
# coloring
scatter_plot_stroke <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1, color = stroke_recode)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, position = position_jitter()) +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL Cholesterol", fill = "Stroke")
plot(scatter_plot_stroke)

# faceting
scatter_plot_stroke2 <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, position = position_jitter()) +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL Cholesterol") +
  facet_wrap(~ stroke_recode)
plot(scatter_plot_stroke2)
```

```{r colors and themes}
# black and white
scatter_plot_bw <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1, color = stroke_recode)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, position = position_jitter()) +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL Cholesterol", color = "Stroke") +
  theme_bw()
plot(scatter_plot_bw)

# classic
scatter_plot_classic <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1, colour = stroke_recode)) + 
                  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, position = position_jitter()) + 
                  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL Cholesterol", colour = "Stroke") +
                  theme_classic()
plot(scatter_plot_classic)

# manual color setting
scatter_plot_manual <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1, colour = stroke_recode)) + 
                  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, position = position_jitter()) + 
                  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9")) +
                  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL Cholesterol", colour = "Stroke") 
plot(scatter_plot_manual)

# Use a ColorBrewer palette 
scatter_plot_brewer <- ggplot(data_all, aes(x = age, y = ldl1, colour = stroke_recode)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, position = position_jitter()) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "LDL Cholesterol", colour = "Stroke") +
  theme_classic()

plot(scatter_plot_brewer)

scatter_plot_brewer + scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2")
scatter_plot_brewer + scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2")
```

```{r heat maps}
data_heat <- data_all %>% select(id, ldl1, ldl2)
head(data_heat)

data_heat <- data_heat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
  gather(-id, key = "key", value = "val") %>% 
  mutate(isna = is.na(val))
head(data_heat)

data_heat2 <- data_all %>%
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
  select(id, ldl1, ldl2) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(ldl1, ldl2),
    names_to = "measurement",
    values_to = "ldl"
  )

# Here, both functions (gather and pivot_longer) reshape data from wide to long format. The column names become values in one new column, and the measurements go into another. The ID stays attached to each measurement.

ggplot(data = data_heat, aes(id, key, fill = val)) +
  geom_tile(alpha=1) +
  labs(x = "Person", y = "LD 1 and 2") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1))

ggplot(data_heat2, aes(x = id, y = measurement, fill = ldl)) +
  geom_tile() +
  labs(x = "Observation", y = "Measurement", fill = "LDL") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Regression stuff

```{r bivariable association}
univ_table <- data_all %>%
  select(ldl1, sex, ethgrp, age, smoking, Cancer, stroke_recode) %>%
  tbl_uvregression( # tbl_uvregression fit a separate model for each predictor, with ldl1 as the outcome
    method = glm,
    y = ldl1,
    method.args = list(family = gaussian)
  )

univ_table

univ_table %>% 
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_caption("**Unadjusted associations with LDL cholestrerol**")

univ_table %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  as_gt() %>%
  gt::tab_options(
    table.font.size = gt::px(14),
    data_row.padding = gt::px(8)
  )

univ_table %>% as_kable()

summary(glm(ldl1 ~ sex, data = data_all))
```

```{r creating a final model}
model_final <- glm(ldl1 ~ sex + ethgrp + age + smoking + Cancer + stroke_recode,
                   data = data_all, 
                   family = "gaussian")

summary(model_final)

str(data_all) #check if categorical variables are well-coded

data_all <- data_all %>%
  mutate(ethnicity = factor(ethgrp),
         cancer_recode = factor(Cancer),
         smoking_recode = factor(smoking))

model_final2 <- glm(ldl1 ~ sex + ethnicity + age + smoking_recode + cancer_recode + stroke_recode, 
                    data = data_all,
                    family = "gaussian")

summary(model_final2)

multi_table <- tbl_regression(model_final)
multi_table2 <- tbl_regression(model_final2)

multi_table %>% as_kable()
multi_table2 %>% as_kable()
```

```{r ploting the final model}
plot_model(model_final, type = "est")

plot_model(model_final2, type = "est")
```

```{r interaction terms}
# Interaction: does the association between smoking and LDL differ by cancer status?
model_interaction <- glm(ldl1 ~ sex + ethgrp + age + smoking*Cancer + stroke_recode,
                         data = data_all,
                         family = "gaussian")
summary(model_interaction)

inter_table <- tbl_regression(model_interaction) 
inter_table %>% as_kable()

plot_interaction <- interact_plot(model_interaction,
                                  pred = smoking, 
                                  modx = Cancer,
                                  plot.points = TRUE,
                                  partial.residuals = TRUE,
                                  interval = TRUE,
                                  int.width = 0.95)

plot(plot_interaction)
```

```{r interaction terms 2}
model_interaction2 <- glm(ldl1 ~ sex + ethnicity + age + smoking_recode*cancer_recode + stroke_recode,
                         data = data_all,
                         family = "gaussian")
summary(model_interaction2)

inter_table2 <- tbl_regression(model_interaction2) 
inter_table2 %>% as_kable()

plot_interaction2 <- interactions::cat_plot(
  model_interaction2,
  pred = smoking_recode,
  modx = cancer_recode,
  interval = TRUE,
  int.width = 0.95
)

plot(plot_interaction2)
```


```{r plot them all together}
# Unadjusted models using the same recoded variables
univ_table2 <- data_all %>%
  select(
    ldl1, sex, ethnicity, age,
    smoking_recode, cancer_recode, stroke_recode
  ) %>%
  tbl_uvregression(
    method = glm,
    y = ldl1,
    method.args = list(family = gaussian())
  )

# Combine the three tables side by side
tbl_univ_multi_inter2 <- tbl_merge(
  tbls = list(univ_table2, multi_table2, inter_table2),
  tab_spanner = c(
    "**Unadjusted**",
    "**Adjusted**",
    "**With interaction**"
  )
)

tbl_univ_multi_inter2
```
